THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. Heard Sri.Hanumanthareddy Sahukar, learned counsel for the appellants and Miss.Vinaya Kuppelur on behalf of Sri.S.S.Koliwad, learned counsel for respondent - Insurance Company.
3. Appeal is by the claimants challenging the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.1209/2014 on the file of Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari dated 27.11.2015.
4.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Admitted facts which are utmost necessary for disposal of this case are as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3415 Parents of Sri.Shaikshavali who lost his life in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.07.2014 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-34/Y-3180 and lorry bearing No.KA-04/A-8456 laid a claim before the Tribunal for awarding suitable compensation.
Charge sheet is filed against the driver of lorry.
5. Tribunal, on contest, allowed the claim petition in a sum of Rs.5,25,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

Validity of the said judgment is in question in the Mehaboob Basah vs Prakash S/O Siddalingappa on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38471655/
2 present appeal.
6.

entities.text: Mehaboob Basah vs Prakash S/O Siddalingappa on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Sri.Hanumanthareddy Sahukar, learned counsel for the appellants reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, contended that the Tribunal has erred in not taking proper income and proper multiplier in view of the settled principles of law enunciated in the cases of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, NC:
2024:KHC-D:3415 United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Others reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076 and Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121 and sought for reassessment of compensation.

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned judgment and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
8. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

9. On such perusal of material on record, death of Sri.Shaikshavali in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.07.2014 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-34/Y- 3180 and lorry bearing No.KA-04/A-8456 as contended by the claimants stands established by placing necessary oral and documentary evidence on record.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3415 10.
Deceased was aged 19 years as on the date of accident.

Therefore, applying the principles of law enunciated in Sarla Verma supra, appropriate multiplier is 18.
11.
In the absence of proper proof of income, Rs.7,500/- should have been taken as monthly income for the accidental death of the year 2014 and 40% should be added towards future prospects.
Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% should be deducted towards personal expenses.

12. Accordingly, a case is made out for reassessment of compensation as under:
Rs.7,500 (income) + 40% (addition) x 12 (months) x 18 (multiplier) x 50%
(deduction)= Rs.11,34,000/-
13.
Claimants are entitled to Rs.11,34,000/- on the head of loss of dependency.
Claimants are also entitled for Rs.30,000/- towards conventional head and claimants being parents, they are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each NC: 2024:KHC-D:3415 towards filial affection.
In all, claimants are entitled to Rs.12,44,000/-.

14. In view of the foregoing discussion, following order is passed:

sentences.text: 3 ORDER
(i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) Impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal stands modified.
(iii) As against Rs.5,25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants are entitled to Rs.12,44,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
(iv) Insurance Company is granted four weeks time to deposit the compensation amount.

Sd/-
